title: One extra S in the URL: what changes for your data on the way? | So That's Why
description:
Little Q is at a café, logging into a game on the free Wi-Fi, and Mom tells her to check first that the address starts with https. But it's just one extra S, isn't it? Doesn't her password still have to be sent out either way?

In this episode, the Chief and Little Q think it through with "passing a letter in class": your password goes through several classmates' hands before it reaches the website. Can the people along the way see it? How do you know the other side really is that website? What does the little lock next to the address mean? And there are things this S doesn't cover at all. Which ones?

The illustrations were made with AI; they are diagrams. The source of every claim is listed in the references below.
